name.en-US: The First Life of St. Francis (Vita prima)
name.pt-BR: Primeira Vida de São Francisco (Vita prima)

description.la: Thomae de Celano Vita prima sancti Francisci (1228-1229), iussu Gregorii IX ante canonizationem scripta: prologus, tria opuscula (vita, ultimi anni et obitus, canonizatio et miracula) et epilogus, cum paragraphis et versibus numeratis.
description.en-US: Thomas of Celano’s First Life of St. Francis (1228-1229), written by order of Gregory IX for the canonization: a prologue, three books (his life; his last years and death; the canonization and miracles) and an epilogue, in the Latin text with paragraph and verse numbers. Titles of the parts and chapters are the source’s. The English is A. G. Ferrers Howell's (1908).
description.pt-BR: A Primeira Vida de São Francisco, por Tomás de Celano (1228-1229), escrita por ordem de Gregório IX para a canonização: prólogo, três livros e epílogo.

la.editor: transcription of the critical text of Fontes Franciscani (1995) by M. Mastrorilli, Politecnico di Bari; edition not stated

sources.edition: Thomas of Celano, Vita prima, poliba.it "Fonti francescane" (Wayback Machine snapshot).
sources.description: Prologue, three opuscula (30 + 10 + 1 chapters), the Miracula and the epilogue, with the source’s paragraph numbers in bold and verse numbers as superscripts. The English of A. G. Ferrers Howell (1908) is OCR only and is not imported.
sources.tierEvidence: Medieval text. The transcription (M. Mastrorilli, Politecnico di Bari, Biblioteca di Scienze del Cristianesimo, 2000-02) survives only in the Wayback Machine; it states no edition, but its biblical apparatus follows Fontes Franciscani (1995). Free in practice, edition unverified.

sources.edition: The Lives of S. Francis of Assisi by Brother Thomas of Celano, translated by A. G. Ferrers Howell (London: Methuen, 1908); archive.org livesofsfranciso00thom, with cu31924101858318 and livessfrancisas00howegoog.
sources.description: Archive.org OCR cleaned by script, not proofread: running heads dropped, Howell's few footnotes kept, his section numbers as inert bold. The drop capital of each chapter's first word, garbled in every scan, is restored by a table read off the scans and checked against the Latin. Howell's Part III runs on without chapters; it is cut at the Latin's sections 127 and 151.
sources.tierEvidence: Printed 1908: public domain in the US.

title.en-US: Chapter II. How God visited his heart by sickness of body and a vision in the night

title.en-US: Chapter III. How, changed in mind but not in body, he spake allegorically of a treasure found, and of a Bride

title.la: Caput IV - Qualiter, venditis omnibus, pecuniam susceptam contempsit.
title.en-US: Chapter IV. How he sold all his goods and despised the money he got for them

title.la: Caput V - Qualiter pater eius persequens ligavit eum.
title.en-US: Chapter V. How his father persecuted and bound him

title.la: Caput VI - Qualiter mater eius solvit eum, et quomodo coram Episcopo Assisii se denudavit.
title.en-US: Chapter VI. How his mother released him, and how he stript himself before the Bishop of Assisi

title.la: Caput VII - Qualiter a latronibus captus, proiectus fuit in nive et quomodo servivit leprosis.
title.en-US: Chapter VII. How he was taken by robbers and thrown into the snow; and how he served the lepers

title.la: Caput VIII - Quomodo construxit ecclesiam Sancti Damiani et de conversatione Dominarum in eodem loco degentium.
title.en-US: Chapter VIII. How he built S. Damian's church: and concerning the conversation of the Ladies who abode in that same place

title.la: Caput IX - Quomodo, mutato habitu, refecit ecclesiam Sanctae Mariae in Portiuncula et audito Evangelio, relictis omnibus habitum quem fratres habent adinvenit et fecit.
title.en-US: Chapter IX. How, having changed his habit, he rebuilt the church of S. Maria in Portiuncula; and how, on hearing the Gospel, he forsook all things, and invented and made the habit which the brethren wear

title.la: Caput X - De preadicatione Evangelii et annuntiatione pacis et sex primorum Fratrum conversione.
title.en-US: Chapter X. Of his preaching of the Gospel and proclamation of peace; and of the conversion of the first six brethren

title.la: Caput XI - De spiritu prophetiae et monitis sancti Francisci.
title.en-US: Chapter XI. Of S. Francis' spirit of prophecy and his admonitions

title.la: Caput XII - Quomodo misit eos binos per mundum, et in brevi tempore iterum congregati sunt.
title.en-US: Chapter XII. How he sent them two by two through the world and how in a short time they came together again

title.la: Caput XIII - Quomodo primo regulam scripsit undecim habens fratres, et quomodo dominus Papa Inocentius eam confirmavit, et de visione arboris.
title.en-US: Chapter XIII. How, having eleven brethren, he first wrote down the Rule; and how the Lord Pope Innocent confirmed it: and concerning the vision of the tree

title.la: Caput XIV - De reditu ipsius ab urbe Roma in vallem Spoletanam et de mora ipsius per viam.
title.en-US: Chapter XIV. Of his return from Rome to the valley of Spoleto, and of his sojourn on the way

title.la: Caput XV - De fama beati Francisci et de conversione multorum ad Deum, et quomodo Ordo vocatus est fratrum Minorum, et qualiter religionem intrantes beatus Franciscus informabat.
title.en-US: Chapter XV. Of the fame of S. Francis, and of the conversion of many to God. How the Order was called that of the Lesser Brethren (Friars Minor); and how blessed Francis fashioned those entering the Religion

title.la: Caput XVI - De mora ipsius apud Rigum Tortum et de custodia paupertatis.
title.en-US: Chapter XVI. Of his sojourn at Rivo Torto and of his guarding of Poverty

title.la: Caput XVII - Quomodo beatus Francicus docuit fratres orare, et de obedientia et puritate fratrum.
title.en-US: Chapter XVII. How the blessed Francis taught the brethren to pray; and concerning the obedience and purity of the brethren

title.la: Caput XVIII - De curru igneo et notitia absentium quam beatus Franciscus habebat.
title.en-US: Chapter XVIII. Of the fiery chariot; and of blessed Francis' knowledge of things absent

title.la: Caput XIX - De custodia qua super fratres vigilabat, et de contemptu sui et vera humilitate.
title.en-US: Chapter XIX. Of S. Francis' watchful guarding of the brethren; of his self-contempt and true humility

title.la: Caput XX - De desiderio quo ad suscipiendum martyrium ferebatur Hispaniam primo, deinde Syriam deambulans, et quomodo Deus per eum nautas de periculo, multiplicatis cibariis liberavit.
title.en-US: Chapter XX. Of the longing whereby he was moved to receive martyrdom, journeying first to Spain and then to Syria: and how God through him delivered the sailors from peril by multiplying the provisions

title.la: Caput XXI - De praedicatione avium et obedientia creaturarum.
title.en-US: Chapter XXI. Of his preaching to the birds and of the obedience of the creatures

title.la: Caput XXII - De praedicatione ipsius apud Esculum, et quomodo per ea quae manu tetigerat, ipso absente, sanabantur infirmi.
title.en-US: Chapter XXII. Of his preaching at Ascoli; and how the sick were healed in his absence by things that his hand had touched

title.la: Caput XXIII - Quomodo claudum apud Tuscanellam et paralyticum apud Narnium sanavit.
title.en-US: Chapter XXIII. How he healed a cripple at Toscanella and a paralytic at Narni

title.la: Caput XXIV - Quomodo mulierem caecam illuminavit et apud Eugubium aliam contractam extendit.
title.en-US: Chapter XXIV. How he gave sight to a blind woman, and at Gubbio straightened another, whose hands were contracted

title.la: Caput XXV - Quomodo fratrem unum a caduco morbo seu a daemonio liberavit, et quomodo apud Sancti Gemini castrum daemoniacam liberavit.
title.en-US: Chapter XXV. How he delivered a brother from the falling sickness, or from a devil; and how he delivered a demoniac woman at the fortress of S. Gemini

title.la: Caput XXVI - Quomodo etiam apud Civitatem de Castello daemonium expulit.
title.en-US: Chapter XXVI. How at Citta di Castello also he cast out a devil

title.la: Caput XXVII - De claritate et constantia mentis eius et de praedicatione coram domino Papa Honorio,et quomodo se et fratres commisit domino Hugoni, episcopo Ostiensi.
title.en-US: Chapter XXVII. Of his serenity and stedfastness of mind and of his preaching before the Lord Pope Honorius; and how he committed himself and the brethren to the Lord Hugo, Bishop of Ostia

title.la: Caput XXVIII - De spiritu charitatis et affectu compassionis quo fervebat erga pauperes, et quid de ove et agniculis fecerit.
title.en-US: Chapter XXVIII. Of the spirit of charity and the compassionate disposition wherewith he glowed toward the poor: and of his treatment of a sheep, and lambs

title.la: Caput XXIX - De amore quem propter Creatorem in omnibus creaturis habebat et de descriptione utriusque hominis sui.
title.en-US: Chapter XXIX. Of the love which he bore to all creatures for the Creator's sake. De- scription of his inner and outer man

title.la: Caput XXX - De praesepio quod fecit in die natalis Domini.
title.en-US: Chapter XXX. Of the manger that he made on Christmas day

title.la: OPUSCULUM SECUNDUM
title.en-US: Part II

title.la: Caput I - De tenore huius opuscoli, de tempore quo S. Franciscus feliciter obiit, et de profectibus ipsius.
title.en-US: Chapter I

title.la: Caput II - De summo desiderio beati Francisci, et qualiter in libri apertione intelexit de se Domini voluntatem.
title.en-US: Chapter II. Of blessed Francis greatest desire; and how in the opening of a book he understood the Lord's will concerning him

title.la: Caput III - De visione hominis imaginem Seraphim crucifixi habentis.
title.en-US: Chapter III. Of the vision of a man having the likeness of a seraph crucified

title.la: Caput IV - De fervore beati Francisci et infirmitate oculorum eius.
title.en-US: Chapter IV. Of blessed Francis' fervour: and of the infirmity of his eyes

title.la: Caput V - Qualiter apud Reatum civitatem receptus fuit a domino Hugone Ostiensi episcopo, et quomodo santus eum pronuntiabat futurum episcopum totius mundi.
title.en-US: Chapter V. How he was received at Rieti by the Lord Hugo, Bishop of Ostia; and how the Saint proclaimed that that bishop would be bishop of all the world

title.la: Caput VI - De moribus fratrum famulantium sancto Francisco, et qualiter ipse disponebat conversari.
title.en-US: Chapter VI. Of the behaviour of the brethren who waited on S. Francis; and how- he was disposing himself to live

title.la: Caput VII - Quomodo de Senis venit Assisium, et de ecclesia Sanctae Mariae de Portiuncula, et de fratrum benedictione.
title.en-US: Chapter VII. How he came from Siena to Assisi: of the Church of Santa Maria in Portiuncula: and of the blessing of the brethren

title.la: Caput VIII - Quid fecerit et dixerit quando feliciter obiit.
title.en-US: Chapter VIII. What he did and said at the time of his happy decease

title.la: Caput IX - Lamentum fratrum et gaudium cum cernerent signa ferentem crucis, et de alis Seraphim.
title.en-US: Chapter IX. Of the brethren's lamentation and of their joy when they beheld him bearing the signs of the Cross: and of the Seraph's wings

title.la: Caput X - De planctu Dominarum apud Sanctum Damianum et quomodo cum laude et gloria sepultus est.
title.en-US: Chapter X. Of the wailing of the ladies at S. Damian; and how S. Francis was buried with praise and glory
